comments.original_text: "Very well." Tuppence helped herself liberally to buttered toast and gave the abridged biography of Miss Prudence Cowley, fifth daughter of Archdeacon Cowley of Little Missendell, Suffolk: ward duties, plate-washing, peeling potatoes, sweeping out wards (where she found a friend of her childhood in Lieutenant Thomas Beresford—bow, Tommy!), then a trade van, a motor-lorry, and a young general. "After that, a Government office, and several enjoyable tea parties—until I was combed out at last. Since then I've been looking for a job. Now—your turn."

comments.original_text: "There's less variety in mine. France, Mesopotamia, wounded again, hospital out there, Egypt till the Armistice, finally demobbed. For ten long, weary months I've been job hunting. There aren't any jobs. And, if there were, they wouldn't give 'em to me. What good am I?"
